Q: What certifications should an LFP battery supplier have for Southeast Asia?A: At minimum, look for CE, UN38.3, and IEC 62619. For specific markets: Malaysia requires SIRIM, Indonesia requires SNI, and Thailand requires TISI. Always request the test report for your exact model and capacity — not a generic brand certificate.Q: How can I tell if a supplier is a real manufacturer or a trading company?A: Request a factory audit report or a live video walkthrough of the production floor. Ask technical questions about cell chemistry and BMS configuration — trading companies usually cannot answer these without consulting a third party.Q: What is a realistic lead time for LFP batteries shipped to Africa?A: Production is typically 4–6 weeks, but shipping to East or West Africa adds another 4–6 weeks due to port congestion and inland logistics. Always build a 50% buffer into any quoted lead time for African destinations.Q: What should an LFP battery warranty cover?A: A reliable warranty should cover manufacturing defects for a minimum of 2 years, allow claims based on photos and test data (not mandatory return shipping to China), and specify the minimum capacity threshold for a valid claim.Q: What is the minimum order quantity for OEM LFP batteries?A: This varies by manufacturer. Legitimate factories typically offer sample orders of 1–5 units for evaluation, with first commercial orders starting from 20–100 units. Be cautious of suppliers requiring 500+ units as a minimum with no flexibility.
